events.title: Vasco da Gama Reaches India
events.description: After rounding the southern tip of Africa and crossing the Indian Ocean, Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama anchored off Calicut on India's Malabar Coast. He was the first European to reach India by sea.
events.significance: The voyage opened a direct maritime trade route between Europe and Asia. It set the stage for Portugal's rise as a global trading power and for centuries of European involvement in the Indian Ocean.

events.title: Christopher Columbus Dies in Valladolid
events.description: The Italian-born navigator who led Spanish voyages across the Atlantic died in Valladolid, Spain. He was about 54 years old, and he was still pressing the Spanish crown to honor the rewards he felt he was owed.
events.significance: Columbus's voyages began lasting contact between Europe and the Americas, a turning point in world history that reshaped continents, economies and peoples.

events.title: Blue Jeans Receive a U.S. Patent
events.description: San Francisco merchant Levi Strauss and Reno tailor Jacob Davis were granted a U.S. patent for work pants reinforced with copper rivets at the stress points.
events.significance: The patent marked the birth of blue jeans, which grew from durable workwear into one of the most recognizable and widely worn garments in the world.

events.title: Lindbergh Takes Off for Paris
events.description: Charles Lindbergh left Roosevelt Field on Long Island, New York, in the single-engine Spirit of St. Louis. He was attempting the first solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic.
events.significance: The flight, which landed in Paris the next day, made Lindbergh a global celebrity. It also gave a major boost to public confidence in air travel and to the aviation industry.
